title: 3.7.8 Lab: Extract a Sub-List with `.slice()`
description: Create an array, copy a middle range and a run to the end with .slice(), then show the original is unchanged. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create the list
steps.instructions: Create a variable called items and assign it an array of at least five values.

steps.title: Extract a middle range
steps.instructions: Use .slice(start, end) to copy a middle part of items into a variable. Remember the end index is not included.

steps.title: Extract to the end
steps.instructions: Use .slice(start) with only a start index to copy everything from a position to the end of the array.

steps.title: Print the results and the original
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print both slices and the original items array, to confirm the original did not change.

requirements.title: Array declared
requirements.description: Declares an array with square brackets. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Declare an array with at least five values in square brackets.

requirements.title: Two .slice() calls
requirements.description: Calls .slice() at least twice. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Call .slice twice: once with a start and an end index, once with only a start. Keep each result in a variable.

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.7.6 (Taking Part of a List with .slice())
requirements.hint: Print both slices and the original items array.

requirements.title: items has five values and the slices and the original are printed
requirements.description: items is an array of at least five values, and at least three lines were printed (two slices and the original). Help: 3.7.6 (Reading: .slice())
requirements.hint: Make items a list of five or more values, take the two slices into their own variables, and print both slices and items.

checks.fail: items should be an array of at least five values, and you should print both slices and the original items array (three lines).
